title: Restriction sections on a contractible specialization neighbourhood
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $V\to X$ be an affine object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. Assume $V$ is weakly contractible, meaning evaluation at $V$ takes every epimorphism of sheaves of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to a surjection, and assume every point of $V$ specializes to a point of $V_Z=V\times_X Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the component at $V$ of the unit $F\to i_*i^{-1}F$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is an isomorphism $F(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}(i^{-1}F)(V_Z)$, natural in $F$.

proof.text: Put $B=V$ and $T=V_Z$. The base-change lemma makes $k:T\hookrightarrow B$ a closed immersion; since $B$ is affine, the affine description of closed immersions gives $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Write $F_B(U\to B)=F(U\to B\to X)$. The localization node identifies $B_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/B$, and likewise $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}/T$. The inverse-image formula gives a canonical identification $(i^{-1}F)|_T\cong k^{-1}F_B$, including the units, as follows. At an object $W\to T$, replace a pair $(E\to X,W\to Z\times_X E)$ in the inverse-image colimit by $(E\times_X B\to B,W\to T\times_B(E\times_X B))$, using the given $W\to T\to B$ and the restriction $F(E)\to F(E\times_X B)$. Conversely forget the map of an object over $B$ to $B$. One composite is identified with the original pair by the projection $E\times_X B\to E$; the other by the graph of the given map to $B$. These arrows also identify the representing sections, so the maps on colimits are mutually inverse. Covers over $W$ are the same in the slice and small sites. The local-sections characterization of sheafification therefore identifies the associated sheaves as well: local representatives and local equalities on either side are exactly those under this presheaf identification. The representative $(B,\mathrm{id}_{T})$ is unchanged, so the original unit at $V$ is the unit for $k$ at $B$.

proof.text: Use the affine ind-etale bases for $k$, with $u(E)=E\times_B T$ and fully faithful $v\dashv u$. Set $L=v(T)$ and let $p:L\to B$ be the counit at the final object $B$ of $B_{\mathrm{app}}$. The functor-properties statement gives $u(L)\cong T$, and $u(p)$ is the identity under this identification (the triangle identity). Thus the image of $p$ contains $T$. The object $L$ is affine and ind-etale over $B$, hence weakly etale and flat. The affine flatness criterion and going down show that its image is closed under generalization: if $b$ specializes to $t\in T$, choose a prime of $L$ over $t$ and lift the prime of $b$ below it. Every $b\in B$ has such a specialization by hypothesis, so $p$ is surjective. A surjective weakly etale map between affines is a one-member pro-etale covering: in the covering definition, over an affine open $D(a)\subset B$ take the affine inverse image $D(p^*a)\subset L$; for any affine open $U\subset B$, choose finitely many basic opens $D(a)\subset U$ covering $U$ by quasi-compactness, and their affine inverse images cover $U$ surjectively. In particular $L\to X$ is a small-site object by weakly etale composition. No unrestricted ring splitting property is inferred from the small-site hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09AC, lemma-compute-i-star, surjectivity argument, corrected to generalization; Tag 09BK, lemma-closed-immersion-affines; Algebra Tag 00HS, lemma-flat-going-down

proof.text: By subcanonicity $h_L$ and $h_B$ are sheaves on the original $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The map $h_L\to h_B$ is locally surjective: an $X$-map $E\to B$ lifts on the pullback covering $E\times_B L\to E$. The epimorphism/local-surjectivity lemma makes it epic. The assumed weak contractibility of $V=B$ now lifts $\mathrm{id}_B\in h_B(B)$ to a morphism $s:B\to L$ with $p s=\mathrm{id}_B$. This is a morphism in $B_{\mathrm{app}}$, because that basis is full and both $B,L$ are its objects. Applying $u$ gives $u(s)=\mathrm{id}_T$ since $u(p)=\mathrm{id}_T$. Hence $u(s p)=\mathrm{id}_T$. On the essential image of fully faithful $v$, the functor $u$ is faithful: the unit $\mathrm{id}\to uv$ is an isomorphism, and adjunction identifies maps between $v$-objects with the corresponding maps between their $u$-images. Thus $s p=\mathrm{id}_L$. Consequently $p$ is an isomorphism. This supplies the uniqueness omitted by Tag 09AC: any other section has the same $u$-image, and its composite with $p$ must again be the identity of $L$, so it equals $s$.

source.place: Tag 09AC, lemma-compute-i-star, existence and omitted uniqueness; Tag 09BK, lemma-closed-immersion-affines; Tag 098Z, lemma-proetale-subcanonical; Sites Tag 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves

proof.text: For a finite covering $\{W_j\to T\}$ in $T_{\mathrm{app}}$, the functor-properties lemma gives a covering $\{v(W_j)\to v(T)=L\cong B\}$. Let $C=\coprod_j v(W_j)$. The finite-coproduct node makes $C$ affine and an object of $B_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and hence of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by weakly etale composition. For any map $E\to B$, the pullback covering by the $v(W_j)$ locally lifts that map to $C$. Subcanonicity and the locally-surjective criterion make $h_C\to h_B$ epic on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Evaluate at $B$ and use its given weak contractibility to obtain a section $B\to C$. Pulling this section back along $T\to B$ gives a section $T\to C\times_B T\cong\coprod_j W_j$ of the disjoint-union covering of $T$. The last identification is literal base change of the components: $u(v(W_j))\cong W_j$, and the inverse images of the disjoint open-and-closed components of $C$ form exactly their disjoint union after base change. We do not assume that $v$ preserves fibre products.

source.place: Tags 09BK/09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines and lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply; Tag 09AC, lemma-compute-i-star, weak-contractibility input

proof.text: The final object $T$ is weakly contractible in $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Indeed, for an epimorphism $P\to Q$ there and $q\in Q(T)$, the local-surjectivity criterion gives local lifts of $q$. The ind-etale basis lemma refines their covering to a finite covering $\{W_j\to T\}$ in $T_{\mathrm{app}}$. Their chosen lifts form a section of $P(\coprod_j W_j)$ by finite-coproduct evaluation, whose image is the restriction of $q$. Pull it back along the section constructed in step 4 to obtain a lift in $P(T)$. This also proves weak contractibility in $T_{\mathrm{app}}$: the basis lemma supplies covering density and its topology is induced; the dense-subsite sheaf equivalence extends an epimorphism of basis sheaves to an epimorphism of full-site sheaves, and both restriction and its inverse preserve epimorphisms by their categorical cancellation definition. Evaluation at the common object $T$ is unchanged. All sites and finite disjoint unions use the fixed small universes, so the equivalence has the smallness hypotheses required for set-valued sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply, clause (2) and its proof; Tag 098X, lemma-affine-alternative; Sites Tag 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves

proof.text: Apply the affine-closed-inverse-image evaluation statement to $k:T\hookrightarrow B$ and the underlying set sheaf of $F_B$. Step 5 verifies its required weak contractibility in $T_{\mathrm{app}}$. It gives $(k^{-1}F_B)(T)\cong F_B(v(T))=F_B(L)$. This is the canonical evaluation of the sheafification of $W\mapsto F_B(v(W))$. In the affine-basis presentation of inverse image (identified with the ordinary inverse image by the cited evaluation statement), adjunction $v\dashv u$ identifies pairs $(E,W\to u(E))$ with maps $v(W)\to E$. The pair $E=v(W)$ with the adjunction unit is final in the indexing direction of restriction maps, so evaluation of that presheaf is $F_B(v(W))$. In particular the representative for the inverse-image unit at $B$ is $E=B$, with $T=u(B)$ and its identity map; its corresponding map $v(T)\to B$ is precisely the counit $p$. Therefore the actual unit component is $F_B(B)\xrightarrow{F_B(p)}F_B(L)$ followed by the canonical sheafification/evaluation isomorphism. Since $p$ is an isomorphism by step 3, this component is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply, clauses (1),(2); Tag 09AC, lemma-compute-i-star; inverse-image unit from Tag 09A5, section-morphism

proof.text: Return through the unit-preserving identification of step 1. It gives the asserted isomorphism $F(V)\to(i^{-1}F)(V_Z)$. All maps used are restriction maps, the prescribed inverse-image colimit maps, and its sheafification unit. They preserve addition on abelian sheaves, so the bijection of underlying sections is an isomorphism of abelian groups. For a morphism $a:F\to F'$, naturality of restriction gives $a_L F(p)=F'(p)a_B$, and naturality of sheafification gives the same commuting square after passing to inverse images. Thus the asserted component is natural in $F$, and it is the original adjunction unit rather than an arbitrary abstract isomorphism.
